chunks: Yunus narrated from Al-Haysam Abu Rawh, the owner of the inn (hotel), who said:

I wrote to Abd Allah ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him): 'I manage hotels, so a man lodges with me and dies suddenly. I do not know him, nor do I know his homeland, nor his heirs. So the wealth remains with me; how should I deal with it, and to whom does that wealth belong?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Leave it in its current state.'

key_terms.عَلَى حَالِهِ: In its current state (preserved as is)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling for the property of a deceased person with no known heirs or identity?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a practical legal ruling for innkeepers regarding the estate of deceased travelers with unknown lineage, instructing them to preserve the wealth rather than distribute it immediately. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of maintaining the status quo (*istishab*) for assets of unknown heirs, ensuring protection against premature disposal while awaiting verification of lineage or further divine instruction.
